payload.title: What Are the Samoan Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.excerpt: Samoan wedding traditions in wedding order, from the families' meeting and the orators' speeches to fine mats, the church service, the taualuga and the feast, with notes for Australians marrying in Samoa or at home.
key_takeaways: A Samoan wedding is led by the aiga, the extended family, and its matai, so the families' wishes shape the day as much as the couple's.
Fine mats ('ie toga) are the highest-ranking item in the Samoan exchange system, and in marriage ceremonies the bride's family presents them to the groom's family.
The church service sits at the heart of the day for many Samoan families, followed by speeches, the siva, the taualuga (the classical Samoan dance) and a shared feast.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises Australians to "Exercise normal safety precautions" in Samoa, and an overseas marriage can't be registered in Australia, though in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.

faq.q: What are the main Samoan wedding traditions?
faq.a: The families' formal meeting and the orators' speeches, the presentation of 'ie toga, the church service, the siva and the taualuga, and a shared feast. Each family keeps its own version, so ask both sides early.

faq.q: Who pays for a Samoan wedding?
faq.a: In many Samoan families, the cost and work are shared across the extended family on both sides, with relatives contributing food, gifts and time. The details are a family conversation, best held before you set the guest list.

faq.q: What is an 'ie toga and why is it given at weddings?
faq.a: An 'ie toga is a finely hand-woven fine mat, the highest-ranking item in the Samoan exchange system. It is displayed and exchanged at weddings and other important gatherings, and its exchange reaffirms kinship ties.
The taualuga is the classical Samoan dance, "a dance of negotiation and celebration". At many weddings the bride dances it as the high point of the reception.

faq.q: What does a Samoan bride wear?
faq.a: Many brides wear a white gown for church and change into a puletasi, a two-piece garment, for the reception, often in fabric that matches the bridal party.

faq.q: What should guests wear to a Samoan wedding?
faq.a: Dress as for church: a dress or blouse and skirt for women, trousers and a shirt for men. Take your shoes off when entering a fale.

faq.q: Can Australians get married in Samoa?
faq.a: An overseas marriage made in Samoa can't be registered in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law; a lawyer can confirm your situation. Check the documents and fees with Samoa's registry and the Australian High Commission in Apia.
